body.title: refactor(logging): replace the logrus backend with log/slog
body.body:
Log through `log/slog`, with a console `slog.Handler` that writes the text the runner has always written (sorted `key=value` fields on a plain stream, a colored prefix on a terminal), so nothing changes for users. I compared its output byte for byte with logrus's `TextFormatter` over plain, colored, timestamped and caller cases.

Libraries that log through logrus's global logger (the workflow model, the Docker client) are forwarded to the process-wide logger, so they keep following its level, format and secret masking. This is why logrus stays in `go.mod`.

Stacked on https://gitea.com/gitea/runner/pulls/1303.

Assisted-by: Codet

body.title: feat(login): support custom HTTP headers per login
body.body:
Allow a login to carry extra HTTP headers that are sent with every request to its server. This makes tea usable with forges behind an authenticating proxy such as Cloudflare Access, which needs CF-Access-Client-Id and CF-Access-Client-Secret service-token headers on each request.

Fixes #990 

## Changes

- Add `headers` to the login config and `Login.BuildTransport()`, which wraps tea's standard transport (timeouts, User-Agent, insecure TLS) with the login's headers. Use it for the SDK client, the raw API client and OAuth token refresh.
- Pass the headers through the OAuth browser flow (token exchange and re-authentication).
- Add a repeatable `--header`/`-H key:value` flag to `tea login add`, so the initial validation request, basic-auth token creation and the `--oauth` flow can reach a server behind the proxy.
- Move `key:value` header parsing into `httputil.ParseHeaders` and reuse it for `tea api --header`.

Headers already set on a request are never overridden. Git operations over HTTPS do not use these transports; use git's `http.extraHeader` for those.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`
- New unit tests for `ParseHeaders` and `WithHeaders`
- Manual: `tea login add -H ...` against a local server that rejects requests without the CF headers

body.title: fix: job container, daemon startup, action cache and exec fixes
body.body:
- Keep `GITHUB_ENV`, `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, `GITHUB_STATE` and `GITHUB_PATH` when a job times out or is cancelled, so post steps still get their state
- Retry the startup Declare while Gitea is unreachable instead of exiting, still failing fast on rejected registrations, auth and misconfiguration
- Reuse a local image when a platform variant such as `linux/arm/v7` is requested instead of pulling again
- Read `PATH` from the created job container so cross-architecture jobs get tool paths for the right architecture
- Extract action copies relative to the act volume so they never cross an image's `/var/run` symlink, which rootless Podman rejects
- Keep the job container's entrypoint when container options set `--entrypoint`, warning instead of appending it to the keep-alive command
- Lock action cache entries across runner processes that share a cache directory
- `exec`: omit `GITHUB_SERVER_URL` and `GITHUB_API_URL` without `--gitea-instance` instead of exporting a bare `https://`, and read owner and repository from any origin remote
